security_audit.summary: All 69 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown, Go syntax, placeholders, documentation links, or benign logging terminology. One medium contextual risk remains because examples enable request-body logging without sensitive-data guidance.

remediation.issue: HTTP middleware examples enable request-body logging without explaining sensitive-data exposure.
remediation.suggestion: Keep body logging disabled by default. Add route filters, strict size limits, and redaction guidance before showing WithRequestBody as enabled.

content.user_title: Build Go Logging Pipelines with samber/slog
content.value_statement: Complex Go logging pipelines can duplicate records, lose buffered events, or expose sensitive data. This skill guides composition, sampling, formatting, middleware, routing, and shutdown.
actual_capabilities: Designs handler pipelines using Fanout, Router, FirstMatch, Failover, Pool, and Pipe.
Places sampling, formatting, routing, and sinks in an efficient order.
Configures threshold, uniform, absolute, and custom sampling strategies.
Applies PII and attribute formatters across downstream handlers.
Configures request logging for Gin, Echo, Fiber, Chi, and net/http.
Explains backend setup, latency behavior, testing, and graceful shutdown.
limitations: Does not replace current package documentation or verify every package version.
Does not provision external logging services, credentials, or network access.
Generated configurations require testing against the installed package versions.
Request and response body logging requires application-specific redaction controls.

use_cases.title: Compose a service logging pipeline
use_cases.description: Create a pipeline that samples noise, masks sensitive attributes, and routes records by level.

use_cases.title: Standardize HTTP request logs
use_cases.description: Configure framework middleware with consistent levels, request identifiers, tracing fields, and filters.

use_cases.title: Diagnose production logging behavior
use_cases.description: Find dropped records, duplicate routing, latency bottlenecks, and missing shutdown flushes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Go slog pipeline using samber/slog-multi. Send error records to Sentry and all records to standard output.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is adopting samber logging handlers.

prompt_templates.title: Add sampling and privacy controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Add threshold sampling and PII formatting to my existing slog pipeline. Explain the handler order and preserve all error records.
prompt_templates.scenario: A service needs lower log volume and safer attributes.

prompt_templates.title: Configure HTTP middleware
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure slog middleware for Gin with distinct 4xx and 5xx levels, request IDs, tracing fields, and health-check filters. Keep body logging disabled.
prompt_templates.scenario: An API team needs consistent request logs.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my samber/slog pipeline for duplicate routing, latency, data exposure, fallback behavior, and shutdown loss. Propose tested changes with tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: An SRE is preparing a logging pipeline for production.

output_examples.input: Why do error records reach both PagerDuty and Slack in my Router?
output_examples.output: The default Router sends each record to every matching handler. Use FirstMatch and order the error rule before the warning rule.

output_examples.input: Where should sampling and PII formatting appear in my pipeline?
output_examples.output: Place sampling first, then apply PII formatting, then route clean records to sinks. Preserve important records with level-aware routing.

output_examples.input: Why are buffered Loki records missing during shutdown?
output_examples.output: The Loki client must stop during graceful shutdown. Register its stop operation and allow enough time to flush pending records.

best_practices: Sample early, format sensitive attributes before routing, and define a catch-all route.
Benchmark handler latency and test routing with in-memory handlers before deployment.
Flush buffered backends during graceful shutdown and verify failures are observable.
anti_patterns: Do not enable request or response body logging without redaction and route exclusions.
Do not assume Router stops after the first matching handler.
Do not use synchronous Fanout when cumulative sink latency is unacceptable.

faq.question: Which Go versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Go 1.21 and later because the packages build on the standard log/slog API.

faq.question: Can it configure multiple logging destinations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains routing, fanout, failover, and pooling across supported samber handlers.

faq.question: Does it prevent sensitive data from entering logs?
faq.answer: It provides formatter patterns for selected attributes. Applications must still identify sensitive fields and avoid unsafe body logging.

faq.question: Does it install Go packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend imports and versions, but dependency changes remain part of the project workflow.

faq.question: Can it validate a production pipeline?
faq.answer: It can review composition and propose tests. Runtime load, backend availability, and package behavior still require direct testing.

faq.question: Why must buffered handlers stop cleanly?
faq.answer: Buffered handlers may retain unsent records. Their stop or close operation flushes pending data before the process exits.
